title: Reading Drill — Reducing repeated journeys to a tool shed — A pilot study
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Reducing repeated journeys to a tool shed — A pilot study
passages.body:
**A** A project in Ravensmere began with reports of gardeners discovering that the right tools are already borrowed. The allotment committee had heard several complaints, but individual reports could not show how often the problem occurred. The team collected evidence using checkout records and chose extra trips per afternoon as its main measure. That allowed it to compare different days using the same rule.

**B** The proposed response was a board listing tools in use. Rather than apply it immediately across the whole site, the team ran a trial in a single area. The trial lasted ten weeks. A second area kept its previous arrangements, making it possible to see whether any change occurred at both sites.

**C** The first review recorded occasional large classes as a factor that could affect the comparison. The team advised repeating the study under different conditions before drawing a wider conclusion. It kept the evidence from the first trial but published a note about why the figures might not apply elsewhere.
